depend.definition: To be controlled, decided, or influenced by someone or something else.
depend.grammar_rule: Always requires the preposition 'on' (or formal 'upon') before a noun or gerund object.
examples: Our weekend plans depend on the weather.
Children depend on their parents for love and security.
depend.common_mistake: ❌ It depends of the situation. ➔ ✅ It depends on the situation.

apologize.definition: To express regret or say sorry for doing something wrong.
apologize.grammar_rule: Use 'to' before the person receiving the apology, and 'for' before the reason or gerund (-ing).
examples: He apologized to his colleagues for being late.
You should apologize for making that remark.
apologize.common_mistake: ❌ He apologized me. ➔ ✅ He apologized to me.

discuss.definition: To talk about something in detail with someone.
discuss.grammar_rule: Strictly transitive direct verb! Do NOT add 'about' after 'discuss'.
examples: We need to discuss the new budget in tomorrow's meeting.
They discussed the problem openly.
discuss.common_mistake: ❌ We discussed about the project. ➔ ✅ We discussed the project.

look forward to.definition: To feel excited or pleased about something that is going to happen.
look forward to.grammar_rule: 'To' is a preposition here, NOT an infinitive marker. Always follow with a noun or -ing verb form.
examples: I look forward to meeting you next week.
She is looking forward to her summer vacation.
look forward to.common_mistake: ❌ I look forward to meet you. ➔ ✅ I look forward to meeting you.

listen.definition: To pay attention to sound or give attention to someone speaking.
listen.grammar_rule: Requires 'to' when followed by an object. Without an object, 'listen' stands alone.
examples: I love listening to jazz music in the evening.
Please listen to the teacher carefully.

accuse.definition: To say that someone has done something wrong or committed a crime.
accuse.grammar_rule: Takes a direct object (the person accused) followed by 'of' + noun/gerund.
examples: They accused him of cheating on the exam.
She was falsely accused of theft.
accuse.common_mistake: ❌ They accused him for stealing. ➔ ✅ They accused him of stealing.

prevent.definition: To stop something from happening or stop someone from doing something.
prevent.grammar_rule: Takes a direct object followed by 'from' + gerund (-ing).
examples: Heavy snow prevented us from leaving the cabin.
Good security measures prevent accidents from occurring.
prevent.common_mistake: ❌ Rain prevented us to go outside. ➔ ✅ Rain prevented us from going outside.

succeed.definition: To achieve a desired aim or result.
succeed.grammar_rule: Requires 'in' + noun or gerund (-ing) when specifying the domain of success.
examples: She succeeded in passing her final exams with top honors.
After months of trial, they succeeded in launching the app.
succeed.common_mistake: ❌ He succeeded to pass the exam. ➔ ✅ He succeeded in passing the exam.

complain.definition: To express dissatisfaction, pain, or annoyance about something.
complain.grammar_rule: Use 'to' for the person/authority receiving complaints, and 'about' or 'of' for the topic/pain.
examples: The customer complained to the manager about the cold food.
He complained of a sudden headache.
complain.common_mistake: ❌ She complained the noise. ➔ ✅ She complained about the noise.

approve.definition: To believe that someone or something is good, acceptable, or suitable.
approve.grammar_rule: 'Approve of' means to hold a favorable opinion. (Note: transitive 'approve' means to give formal authorization).
examples: Her parents didn't approve of her choice of career.
Do you approve of working overtime on weekends?
approve.common_mistake: ❌ I don't approve your behavior. ➔ ✅ I don't approve of your behavior.

insist.definition: To demand something forcefully, not accepting refusal.
examples: He insisted on paying for the whole dinner.
They insist on absolute punctuality.
insist.common_mistake: ❌ She insisted to pay the bill. ➔ ✅ She insisted on paying the bill.

belong.definition: To be the property of or be a member/part of something.
belong.grammar_rule: Always followed by 'to' when indicating ownership or organization membership.
examples: This antique watch belonged to my grandfather.
Which sports club do you belong to?
belong.common_mistake: ❌ This book belongs me. ➔ ✅ This book belongs to me.

rely.definition: To trust or depend on someone or something with confidence.
examples: You can always rely on David to keep a secret.
Modern businesses rely heavily on digital communication.
rely.common_mistake: ❌ Don't rely in luck. ➔ ✅ Don't rely on luck.

marry.definition: To become the legally accepted husband or wife of someone.
marry.grammar_rule: Active verb is transitive direct (no preposition). Passive 'be married to' uses 'to'.
examples: She married her high school sweetheart last month.
Will you marry me?
marry.common_mistake: ❌ He married with a famous actress. ➔ ✅ He married a famous actress.

enter.definition: To come or go into a place.
enter.grammar_rule: Direct object when referring to physical places. (Note: 'enter into an agreement' is a phrasal idiom).
examples: Please knock before you enter the room.
The thief entered the house through the back window.
enter.common_mistake: ❌ She entered into the classroom. ➔ ✅ She entered the classroom.

reach.definition: To arrive at a place, achieve a milestone, or contact someone.
reach.grammar_rule: Transitive direct object without preposition. Do NOT use 'at' or 'to'.
examples: We reached the hotel late in the evening.
They finally reached a consensus.
reach.common_mistake: ❌ We reached to the top of the hill. ➔ ✅ We reached the top of the hill.

congratulate.definition: To express praise and joy to someone for their achievement or good fortune.
congratulate.grammar_rule: Takes a direct object (the person) followed by 'on' + achievement.
examples: I congratulated her on her promotion.
We congratulated the team on winning the tournament.
congratulate.common_mistake: ❌ I congratulated him for his success. ➔ ✅ I congratulated him on his success.

blame.definition: To assign responsibility or fault to someone or something.
blame.grammar_rule: Two valid structures: 'blame PERSON for THING' or 'blame THING on PERSON'.
examples: Don't blame him for the mistake.
She blamed the accident on the slippery road.
blame.common_mistake: ❌ Don't blame on him for this. ➔ ✅ Don't blame him for this.

concentrate.definition: To direct all your attention and efforts toward a single activity.
concentrate.grammar_rule: Requires 'on' before the subject of focus or action.
examples: I need a quiet place to concentrate on my studies.
Concentrate on breathing deeply.
concentrate.common_mistake: ❌ He concentrated in his work. ➔ ✅ He concentrated on his work.

focus.definition: To pay central attention to a topic, or direct light/effort onto an object.
focus.grammar_rule: Can be intransitive ('focus on X') or transitive ('focus attention on X'). Always uses 'on'.
examples: The presentation focuses on sustainable energy.
She focused her camera on the flying eagle.
focus.common_mistake: ❌ Let's focus in the main issue. ➔ ✅ Let's focus on the main issue.

consist.definition: To be composed or made up of specified parts or elements.
consist.grammar_rule: Use 'consist of' for physical/constituent components. Use 'consist in' for defining features.
examples: The team consists of five experienced engineers.
True happiness consists in being satisfied with what you have.
consist.common_mistake: ❌ The salad consists from tomatoes and cucumbers. ➔ ✅ The salad consists of tomatoes and cucumbers.

suffer.definition: To experience physical or mental pain, illness, or disadvantage.
suffer.grammar_rule: Intransitive 'suffer from' takes illness/pain. Transitive direct 'suffer' takes abstract loss (e.g. suffer defeat/losses).
examples: Many people suffer from seasonal allergies in spring.
The company suffered heavy financial losses.
suffer.common_mistake: ❌ He suffers with asthma. ➔ ✅ He suffers from asthma.

remind.definition: To cause someone to remember something or resemble someone.
remind.grammar_rule: Direct object (person) followed by 'of' + noun, or followed by 'to' + infinitive.
examples: This song reminds me of my college days.
Please remind me to call the accountant later.
remind.common_mistake: ❌ This reminds me about my hometown. ➔ ✅ This reminds me of my hometown.

warn.definition: To inform someone in advance of possible danger, risk, or problem.
warn.grammar_rule: Direct object (person) followed by 'about/of' + noun or 'against' + gerund (-ing).
examples: The weather report warned us about the upcoming storm.
Doctors warn against eating too much processed sugar.
warn.common_mistake: ❌ They warned us to not swim. ➔ ✅ They warned us against swimming / not to swim.

charge.pattern: charge [someone] with [a crime] OR charge [someone] [money] for [a service]
charge.definition: To formally accuse someone of a crime, or demand a price for goods/services.
charge.grammar_rule: 'Charge with' for legal accusation; 'charge for' for financial payment.
examples: Police charged the suspect with armed robbery.
The garage charged us $200 for the car repairs.
charge.common_mistake: ❌ He was charged of theft. ➔ ✅ He was charged with theft.

borrow.definition: To take and use something belonging to someone else, intending to return it.
borrow.grammar_rule: Direct object (item) followed by 'from' + owner. (Do NOT confuse with 'lend').
examples: Can I borrow a pen from you?
She borrowed three books from the library.
borrow.common_mistake: ❌ Can I borrow to you a pen? ➔ ✅ Can I borrow a pen from you?

lend.definition: To give something to someone for a temporary period.
lend.grammar_rule: Dual object structure: direct item + 'to' + receiver, or receiver + direct item.
examples: I lent my bicycle to my brother.
Could you lend me some money until Friday?
lend.common_mistake: ❌ He lent me from his car. ➔ ✅ He lent me his car.

protect.definition: To keep someone or something safe from harm, injury, or loss.
examples: Sunscreen protects your skin from harmful UV rays.
Vaccines protect against severe infectious diseases.
protect.common_mistake: ❌ Protect your skin to the sun. ➔ ✅ Protect your skin from the sun.

substitute.definition: To use or put something in place of another.
substitute.grammar_rule: Takes new item A, followed by 'for' + original item B.
examples: You can substitute olive oil for butter in this recipe.
The coach substituted a younger player for the fatigued veteran.
substitute.common_mistake: ❌ Substitute apples with oranges (when putting apples in). ➔ ✅ Substitute apples for oranges.

replace.definition: To take the place of or substitute something with another.
replace.grammar_rule: Takes original item A, followed by 'with' + new item B.
examples: We replaced our old television with a modern 4K screen.
Coal heating is being replaced by renewable energy.
replace.common_mistake: ❌ Replace the old model for a new one. ➔ ✅ Replace the old model with a new one.

search.definition: To look carefully in order to find someone or something.
search.grammar_rule: 'Search for X' means seeking item X. 'Search X' means physically examining place X.
examples: They searched for their lost keys everywhere.
Customs officers searched the suspicious luggage.
search.common_mistake: ❌ He searched his keys. ➔ ✅ He searched for his keys.

run.definition: To move quickly on foot (intransitive), or operate/manage a business (transitive).
run.grammar_rule: Intransitive in movement; transitive direct when managing an organization.
examples: She runs five miles every morning.
He has been running a successful startup for three years.
run.common_mistake: ❌ He runs of a company. ➔ ✅ He runs a company.

stop.pattern: stop [doing something] (gerund) vs stop to [do something] (infinitive purpose)
stop.definition: To halt motion, action, or operation.
stop.grammar_rule: Gerund means quit action entirely. Infinitive means pause current activity to do another.
examples: He stopped smoking three years ago.
On the drive home, we stopped to buy groceries.
stop.common_mistake: ❌ He stopped to smoke (when quitting). ➔ ✅ He stopped smoking.

change.grammar_rule: Intransitive (the situation changes) or transitive direct (you change something). Uses 'into' for transformation.
examples: The caterpillar changed into a beautiful butterfly.
You need to change your password regularly.
change.common_mistake: ❌ Change to another clothes. ➔ ✅ Change into other clothes.

prefer.definition: To like one thing or person better than another.
prefer.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' when comparing two options with 'prefer', NEVER 'than'.
examples: I prefer tea to coffee in the morning.
She prefers walking to driving in heavy traffic.
prefer.common_mistake: ❌ I prefer tea than coffee. ➔ ✅ I prefer tea to coffee.

differ.definition: To be unlike or distinct in nature, quality, or form.
differ.grammar_rule: Use 'differ from' for dissimilarity; 'differ in' for the point of distinction.
examples: British English differs from American English in spelling and vocabulary.
The two models differ mainly in battery capacity.
differ.common_mistake: ❌ This approach differs than mine. ➔ ✅ This approach differs from mine.

depend on.definition: To rely on or be contingent upon.
depend on.grammar_rule: Standard phrasal combination with required preposition 'on'.
examples: Our survival depends on clean water.
Success depends on hard work.
depend on.common_mistake: ❌ Depends to you. ➔ ✅ Depends on you.

talk.definition: To speak in order to give information or express feelings.
examples: I need to talk to you about the project.
She spent an hour talking with her sister.
talk.common_mistake: ❌ Talk the teacher. ➔ ✅ Talk to the teacher.

speak.definition: To utter words, communicate orally, or know a language.
speak.grammar_rule: Transitive when naming a language ('speak fluent French'); intransitive with 'to/with' for people.
examples: She speaks four foreign languages fluently.
May I speak to Mr. Henderson, please?

explain.definition: To make something clear or easy to understand by describing it.
explain.grammar_rule: The listener MUST be preceded by 'to', even if placed before the topic.
examples: Can you explain this rule to me?
The professor explained the theory to the class.
explain.common_mistake: ❌ Explain me this problem. ➔ ✅ Explain this problem to me.

describe.definition: To give a detailed account in words of someone or something.
describe.grammar_rule: Transitive direct verb for topic; use 'to' for the listener.
examples: She described her trip to her friends.
The witness described the suspect to police officers.
describe.common_mistake: ❌ Describe to me your car. ➔ ✅ Describe your car to me.

suggest.definition: To put forward an idea, plan, or option for consideration.
suggest.grammar_rule: Never followed by an indirect object without 'to'. Takes gerund or 'that' clause.
examples: I suggested going for a walk.
He suggested a solution to the manager.
suggest.common_mistake: ❌ She suggested me a restaurant. ➔ ✅ She suggested a restaurant to me.

recommend.definition: To advise or praise something as being suitable for a particular purpose.
recommend.grammar_rule: Takes gerund or direct object; listener requires 'to'.
examples: The doctor recommended taking a rest.
Can you recommend a good hotel to us?
recommend.common_mistake: ❌ He recommended me a book. ➔ ✅ He recommended a book to me.

wait.definition: To stay in a place or delay action until something expected happens.
wait.grammar_rule: Requires 'for' when specifying the target of waiting. (Compare with transitive 'await').
examples: We waited for the bus for thirty minutes.
She is waiting for her exam results.

avert.definition: To turn away or prevent an undesirable event from happening.
avert.grammar_rule: Direct object required; use 'from' when turning gaze or focus away.
examples: He averted his eyes from the gruesome accident.
Prompt emergency response averted a major catastrophe.
avert.common_mistake: ❌ Avert off the crisis. ➔ ✅ Avert the crisis.

attribute.definition: To regard something as being caused by a specific person or factor.
attribute.grammar_rule: Requires direct object (effect) followed by 'to' + cause.
examples: The doctor attributes her quick recovery to good nutrition.
Historians attribute the collapse to economic instability.
attribute.common_mistake: ❌ Attribute the success for hard work. ➔ ✅ Attribute the success to hard work.

refrain.definition: To stop oneself from doing or enjoying something.
examples: Please refrain from smoking inside the terminal.
Passengers are asked to refrain from using mobile devices during takeoff.
refrain.common_mistake: ❌ Refrain to speak during the exam. ➔ ✅ Refrain from speaking during the exam.

abstain.definition: To formally choose not to vote, or restrain oneself from indulging.
abstain.grammar_rule: Requires 'from' before the activity or vote.
examples: Ten members voted in favor, two against, and three abstained from voting.
Athletes should abstain from alcohol during training.
abstain.common_mistake: ❌ Abstain of voting. ➔ ✅ Abstain from voting.

dedicate.definition: To devote time, effort, or a work of art to a specific purpose or person.
dedicate.grammar_rule: Followed by 'to' (preposition). When followed by a verb, use the gerund (-ing).
examples: She dedicated her life to helping underprivileged children.
The author dedicated his latest book to his late mother.
dedicate.common_mistake: ❌ Dedicated to help others. ➔ ✅ Dedicated to helping others.

commit.pattern: commit [a crime] (VT) / commit oneself to [gerund] (VT reflexive)
commit.definition: To carry out an action, or pledge loyalty/time to a cause.
commit.grammar_rule: 'Commit to' takes a gerund (-ing) or noun object.
examples: The company committed to reducing carbon emissions by 50%.
He committed a grave error during the interview.
commit.common_mistake: ❌ Committed to reduce pollution. ➔ ✅ Committed to reducing pollution.
